agent_notes: In the Hebrew numbering the superscription is verse 1 (KJV 8:0), so every later verse is one higher than in the KJV. The meaning of 'al-haggittith is unknown; I give the two main ancient guesses (an instrument or tune from Gath, per Rashi/Metzudat Zion; a vintage/winepress song, per the 'treaders' reading in Rashi and Ibn Ezra) and commit to neither.

STEPBible glosses lamnatsea'h 'to the choirmaster'; I kept 'to the choirmaster' and say in the commentary that the sense of the root (to lead, to be pre-eminent) is a liturgical role, not a title we can fix.

agent_notes: Revised per the reviewer request. tenah is a crux: Radak, Ibn Ezra and Meiri take it as an infinitive standing for the past (Meiri also reads asher as 'if', which I did not follow); Metzudat Zion takes it as an imperfect used for the past ('you gave'). I render it as a past act in the dramatic layer and keep the oddity of the form in the literal layer.

Gloss for token 9 (teNah) corrected from STEPBible 'set !' to 'to set / you set' to reflect the infinitive-or-past reading. Token 8 'asher' is glossed 'which', since English 'who' would settle whether it refers to God or to the name.

elohim: the five English versions split (KJV and Webster 'angels', ASV 'God', BBE 'the gods', YLT 'Godhead'). Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri, Metzudat David and the Targum all take it as angels. I keep 'God' in the literal layer because the word is the plural-form divine title, and note the traditional reading in the commentary. STEPBible tags the token as deity.yhwh; I left that to the entity layer.
